outcomes.query: our point-in-time copies keep ballooning in size because every run folds the prior archive into the new one over and over
outcomes.judgeNotes: The top-1 memory retrieval result is completely irrelevant to the stated intent. The intent concerns point-in-time archive copies growing unboundedly because each run re-embeds the prior archive into the new one (a snowball/nesting problem). The returned memory is a project-topology reference card covering repo paths, a browser-based VSCode URL pattern, a Starlight docs viewer URL, and overmind process management — none of which has any bearing on archiving strategy, snapshot accumulation, or deduplication. This is a prototypical lexical-gap failure: the query's domain vocabulary (point-in-time copies, archive folding, size ballooning) shares no surface tokens with the stored memory's vocabulary (harness, HarnessDashboard, code-server, Starlight, overmind), so the backend ranked an unrelated card at the top.

outcomes.query: [boot-migrate] FAILED 000-baseline.sql: must be owner of function task_lineage
outcomes.judgeNotes: The top retrieval result partially addresses the intent by mentioning the exact error string and labeling it as 'benign noise on boot that is NOT the crash cause,' but the result's primary content is about an unrelated systemd working-directory crash-loop. The relevant fact is buried at the tail of a long memory about a different failure mode, and no information is provided about the actual ownership issue (PostgreSQL function ownership, migration sequencing, or how to resolve it if desired). An agent acting on this intent would learn the error can be safely ignored in this particular setup, but would not understand why it occurs or how to fix it in a fresh environment.

outcomes.query: running e2e tests for the Papercusp desktop app
outcomes.judgeNotes: The top memory result is directly and specifically useful for the stated intent of running e2e tests for the Papercusp desktop app. It names the exact CLI tool to use (tauri-agent-tools), provides the canonical documentation path, explains the pre-flight command, covers the most common failure mode (bridge discovery), and warns against known anti-patterns (curl, xdotool). An agent acting on this intent would be immediately actionable without any additional context.
